issues.title: art: regen the endgame poster batch under the provisional rules, THEN decide which rules survive
issues.body:
From the 2026-07-29 spoken review of the endgame concept batch (Pip + Wanasai, 34 min). Full extraction with per-concept verdicts and the ten rules: `docs/art/ENDGAME_CONCEPT_REVIEW_2026-07-29.md`.

Ticketed deliberately, because the lesson of the same day was that a commitment recorded only in prose does not get scheduled (see #1018).

## The order matters

1. Fold rules **A1-A10 into the manifest's shared style block as PROVISIONAL**, so they apply by construction rather than by anyone remembering them.
2. Regenerate the keepers under those rules -- **no people** is the default.
3. **Then review the rules against the output** and decide which are real.

Step 3 is the point of this issue. Pip's ruling:

> "some of the rules here might be more like guidelines and I don't want to over-commit future me without a generation of regens at least"

So: **do not promote any of A1-A10 into `UI_STYLE_GUIDE.md`, an ADR, or the glossary before one full regen cycle has run.** After it, promote what demonstrably improved the output, demote what merely narrowed it, and kill anything that made the art worse.

**A2 (no people in poster art) is the one to watch.** It is the most sweeping rule and the most likely to be over-broad -- it may turn out to mean "no *incidental* people" rather than "no people". It is also a genuine insight about the game's thesis (people in frame imply a protagonist, and this is a game about everyone else), so it should not be dismissed cheaply either. That tension is exactly what a regen cycle resolves and argument does not.

The one exception safe to land early: **A9**, that the correct term is *poster art* rather than hero art. That is a naming correction, not a taste judgement.

## Batch outcome for reference

- **Keep / rework (9):** orbital_datacenter_ring (V1, extended further through the composition), cheerful_propaganda_atrium (generate with and without a face -- Pip and Wanasai disagreed), chokehold_water_and_gigawatts (hybrid: V1 composition + pipe, V2 colour, less electricity), chokehold_permit_counter, crux_drone_arms_race, defeated_drone_coolant (V2, no cockpit), economics_rung_shuttered_street (V2), attention_loud_vs_slow (V2), intro_bus_strangers_help (V2, hero must stay unidentifiable)
- **Hard pass (4):** same_desire_two_field_strengths, attention_stack_buried_desk, field_leaks_at_every_angle, pacification_delivery_suburb
- **Still open (2):** field_ladder_three_rungs variant; remote_operators_room, which is blocked on how A2 resolves

## Two things worth carrying forward

**The best idea in the session was a salvage, not an image.** Robots all facing one way implies a camera and therefore a protagonist. The replacement concept -- you order one TV and twenty robots arrive with twenty TVs, then twenty fridges the next day, explicitly the horror of an unbounded `for` loop -- is stronger than the image it replaces and wants its own concept id.

**The generating agent's self-nominated best image was hard-passed as cliche** (`attention_stack_buried_desk`). Useful calibration for any future batch where an agent reports which of its outputs is strongest.

issues.title: LEAGUE-CRITICAL: game does not initialise on launch -- full UI, Phase: Not Started, no action buttons
issues.body:
Observed by Pip 2026-07-29 ~22:14 AEST, running from source at `3f408038` (the frozen 0.13.2 content). **This is the first thing Thursday morning should touch**, because [Gate 4: PROVEN BUILD] requires "a human has played the thing we ship" -- and right now the thing does not start.

Not a playtest gap. The systems could not be tested because no run was ever created.

## Symptom

Game launches, main scene loads, all chrome renders -- and then nothing is live:

- Feed reads `Game not started...`
- Footer reads `Phase: Not Started`
- **No action buttons in the left-hand column at all**
- `Money $0`, `Compute 0`, `Research 0`, `Papers 0`, `Rep 0`, `AP: 0`
- Action Queue: `No actions queued...`
- Office scene, cat (Mando), doom readout (58.5%) and upgrades panel all render normally

So the presentation layer is entirely healthy and the game state is absent.

## Log evidence

The launch path completes without an error. Relevant lines:

```
[ConfigConfirmation] Launching game...
[GameConfig] Games played: 97
[SceneTransition] go_to(res://scenes/main.tscn) queued (fade=false)
[PerfLog][WARN] SLOW section 'scene_load' took 2887.6 ms (threshold 1000 ms)  { "target": "res://scenes/main.tscn" }
[OfficeCat] Loaded cat image: Mando (res://assets/cats/simple/web-mando.jpg)
[TabManager] Showing main screen
[PauseMenu] Initializing...
[DebugOverlay] Ready - Press F3 to toggle
```

Note what is ABSENT: no `[GameManager] Starting new game`, and no player/lab/seed/difficulty block, which `start_new_game()` prints unconditionally once it gets past its guard. **`start_new_game()` either was never called or returned early.**

## Leading hypothesis

`game_manager.gd:46` `start_new_game(game_seed, force)` carries a self-guard added in the scene-reentry run-killer family (sibling of #979):

```gdscript
if is_initialized and not force:
    push_warning("[GameManager] start_new_game() REFUSED: ...")
    PerfLog.mark("start_new_game_refused", ...)
    return
```

The docstring says legitimate fresh-start callers -- "the welcome/config_confirmation Launch-Lab chain via main_ui._boot_game's fresh-boot branch" -- pass `force=true` explicitly. The observed state is exactly what a refused call produces: UI constructed, state never initialised.

The `push_warning` does not appear in the captured console output, which weakens but does not kill the hypothesis (warnings may not surface identically in that stream). **Check `PerfLog` for a `start_new_game_refused` mark -- that is the decisive evidence**, at `C:/Users/Pip/AppData/Roaming/Godot/app_userdata/P(Doom)/logs/perf.log`.

Second candidate: an ordering problem. `scene_load` took **2887 ms** against a 1000 ms threshold -- an unusually wide window for a boot-sequence assumption to break in.

Third: an artefact of running from source with a warm `.godot` rather than a real build. Cheap to rule out, and worth ruling out FIRST because it changes the severity completely.

## Why this is league-critical

Friday's league runs on this content. If it reproduces on the built artifact, there is no league. Bugfixes labelled league-critical are explicitly permitted past [Gate 2: THE FREEZE], which was declared at 22:28 tonight.

## Thursday morning triage order

1. Reproduce from a **built artifact**, not from source. If it does not reproduce, severity drops sharply and this becomes an editor-path bug.
2. Grep `perf.log` for `start_new_game_refused`.
3. Check whether `main_ui._boot_game()`'s fresh-boot branch passes `force=true` on this path.
4. Note that games_played incremented to 97, so the config chain completed fully -- the failure is downstream of config, at or after scene load.

Reported with full console log; ask Pip for the paste if needed.

issues.title: fix(release): semver-sort the release feed -- it has called v0.9.0 "latest" since v0.10.0 (#1008)
issues.body:
#1008 said the release index is hand-maintained because CI throws the generated feed away. That's true, but it isn't the root cause. **The generator itself produced the wrong answer**, so committing its output — the issue's own proposed fix — would have shipped the same bug.

## Root cause

```python
tags.sort(reverse=True)     # scripts/generate_release_metadata.py
```

A plain string sort. Lexicographically **`"v0.9.0" > "v0.13.1"`** because `9 > 1` at the third character, and `generate_releases_index()` takes `releases[0]` as `latest_version`.

**So the feed has reported v0.9.0 as the newest release since v0.10.0 shipped.** The tracked index bore it out: one entry, `generated_at` 2025-11-08, download URLs pointing at `PDoom.exe` — the same nonexistent asset the README advertised until #1013. The website consumes this feed, so this was player-visible.

## Three fixes

1. **`_semver_sort_key()`** — numeric sort. A bare `vX.Y.Z` outranks `vX.Y.Z-suffix` at the same version, so a hotfix tag never displaces the release it patches. Unparseable tags sort last rather than raising, so a stray tag can't break a release run.
2. **`_ascii_safe()`** on the generated `changelog` and `tag_message` fields. Historical tag messages carry emoji and mojibake (`U+00F0`, `U+00EF` — lone leading bytes of UTF-8 emoji), which made the regenerated feed **unstageable** against the ASCII-only gate (#744). Worth knowing: this would have broken any CI job that commits the feed back, which is #1008's other proposed fix.
3. **`--check`** — writes nothing, exits 1 when the tracked index disagrees with the git tags. Wired into pre-commit, mirroring `sync_version.py --check` and `generate_dq_index.py --check`, which is the anti-rot pattern the issue asks for.

## Result

**21 releases, correctly ordered, latest v0.13.1** (was: 1 release, latest v0.9.0). Backfills v0.13.0/v0.13.1 per #1008 item 3, which matters this week — Friday's build lands in this feed.

## Design notes on `--check`

Compares **semantics** (which releases, what order, which is latest), not bytes: the files carry a `generated_at` timestamp that changes every run, so a byte comparison would fail constantly and train everyone to bypass the hook. Scoped to `public/releases/` so it only fires when the feed is touched — a full-tree gate would block every commit after a tag until someone regenerated.

Proven both ways: exit 0 on the regenerated index; exit 1 on the stale one, naming all 20 missing tags.

## Deliberately not included

Unmuting the `verify_release_urls --sweep` step (#1008 item 2). The v0.9.0 entry's URLs really are dead, so making the sweep blocking tonight would fail Friday's release workflow on a 2025 artifact. It wants the #1007 treatment — loud, not blocking. Left on #1008.

Tooling and data only; no mechanics. Permitted past [Gate 2: THE FREEZE].

Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

issues.title: ADR-0005 seed schedules are INERT in real play: nothing passes a schedule to GameState, so event_schedule is always empty
issues.body:
Found 2026-07-29 while checking whether a hand-authored league pack could be shipped for Friday. It cannot, and the reason is more interesting than the pack.

## The finding

`GameState._init(game_seed, schedule)` accepts a schedule and treats it as part of seed identity:

```gdscript
func _init(game_seed: String = "", schedule: Array = []):
	# WS-C (ADR-0005): schedule is part of seed identity; duplicated so external mutation
	# can't alias it, and deliberately NOT cleared by reset().
	event_schedule = schedule.duplicate(true)
```

But the live-play callsite passes nothing:

```gdscript
# godot/scripts/game_manager.gd:80
state = GameState.new(game_seed)
```

The only callers that pass a schedule are `baseline_simulator.gd:228`, `replay_simulator.gd:56`, and `save_load.gd:92` (which restores whatever was saved -- i.e. an empty array).

**So `event_schedule` is `[]` for every real run.** `SeedSchedule.apply_due_causes()` iterates an empty array once per turn and has never fired a cause for a player.

## Why this matters beyond the pack

1. **ADR-0005's variance mechanism is unexercised in the shipped game.** "A seed = RNG seed + event schedule" is true of the data model and false of every game anyone has played.
2. **Board and replay identity carry an always-empty half.** `verification_tracker.gd` records `event_schedule` as part of run identity; `game_state.gd:1444` serialises it as "part of seed identity". Both are faithfully recording nothing.
3. **Nothing in the docs says so.** ADR-0005, ADR-0016 and the glossary all read as though schedules are live content. This is the declared-vs-actual drift pattern again (see #1018).

## What was actually missing all along

Not a schema. `seed_schedule.gd` has always defined the cause shape --
`{"turn": int, "cause": String, "target": String, "magnitude": float}` -- with three INPUT-only cause types (`rival_funding_wave`, `rival_aggression_shift`, `inject_event`) and the ADR-0005 "author causes, never outcomes" invariant enforced in code with a guard test.

**A pack is just a list of those causes.** The missing piece is a **loader**: something that reads a pack file and hands the array to `GameState.new()` at `game_manager.gd:80`.

Note the pleasant consequence: because the three cause types can only touch sim INPUTS, [Gate 3: PACK BLESSED]'s "zero printed doom deltas" check is satisfied **by construction**. The format cannot express printed doom. The grep is a belt over a structural guarantee.

## Scope of the fix (NOT for this league)

- [ ] Decide where packs live (`godot/data/packs/<id>.json`?) and how one is selected -- per league? per seed? A pack is part of seed identity, so selection must be deterministic and recorded.
- [ ] Load the pack and pass it at `game_manager.gd:80`.
- [ ] Ensure the loaded schedule reaches `VerificationTracker` so replays still verify.
- [ ] Validate cause types on load, rejecting unknown ones loudly rather than `push_warning` at fire time.
- [ ] Decide the ladder consequence explicitly: changing pack content changes what fires on a fixed seed, so **every pack change forks the ladder**. This contradicts ADR-0016's "monthly, light... mild lore and sprint refresh" framing -- see #1018.

## Why not now

This is gameplay code, and gameplay is exactly what [Gate 2: THE FREEZE] (PR #1019) freezes. The Friday league ships **pack-free**, which costs nothing it was ever actually getting: an empty schedule is what every previous league ran on too.

Candidate epoch: v0.14 (Aug 7), alongside the ADR-0016 correction.

issues.title: Philosophy Quest: progressive supersession scan over the ADR set + stricter admission rules
issues.body:
Articulated by Pip 2026-07-29 15:43, deliberately NOT to be resolved now. Filed immediately because the lesson of the same afternoon is that **an unticketed commitment does not get scheduled** (see the pack-schema post-mortem below).

## The diagnosis

The repo has **no supersession mechanism**. ADRs are append-only in practice. A later decision does not know which earlier one it invalidates, and nothing marks the earlier one as superseded. The result is a set of mutually-contradicting documents that all read ACCEPTED.

This is not hypothetical. Collisions found in a single day, mostly as side effects of writing a glossary:

| Collision | Evidence |
|---|---|
| **ADR-0016 vs RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE** | ADR-0016 (07-13) calls world-updates "monthly, light... a mild lore and sprint refresh" and "decoupled" from balance patches. But `seed_schedule.gd:3` states a seed = RNG seed + event schedule, so changing schedule content changes what happens on a fixed seed -- which the CANONICAL fork rule (07-25) says MUST fork the ladder. There is no such thing as a light world update. ADR-0016 is superseded in substance while still reading ACCEPTED. |
| **The split spec's own ADR number** | `BUILD_VS_LADDER_VERSION_SPLIT.md` says "Status: DRAFT... recommend promoting to ADR-0018" -- but ADR-0018 is taken by the render-only office doctrine, and the split is fully IMPLEMENTED and live in `game_config.gd`. A live system's spec still reads DRAFT and points at an occupied number. |
| **Ladder columns off by one** | `ROADMAP.md` and `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md` both map v0.14 -> L3, but L3 was spent mid-month by #982. Every row from v0.14 down is wrong. |
| **Stale runtime comment** | `game_config.gd:159-160` reads "Epoch L1 == the current ruleset" and predicts a bump "to 2 at the v0.13 epoch cut", directly above a const reading `"3"`. |
| **The index itself** | `decisions/README.md` is hand-maintained and stale. CLAUDE.md already warns readers to trust the ADR files and not the index -- a documented workaround for a broken artifact. |
| **`L<n>` overloaded** | Ladder epochs L1/L2/L3 vs the distribution update ladder L0-L3. Same notation, unrelated meanings, both spoken in league week. |

## The generator

Each ADR is a correct snapshot of a decision at a moment. Nothing carries the *edges between* decisions. So the set accumulates truth-at-a-time and presents it as truth-now, and the contradictions are invisible until someone reads two documents in the same hour.

Note what surfaced them: **writing a glossary.** Forcing one meaning per term across documents is what made the disagreements legible. That is a reusable technique, not a one-off.

## The repo already contains the fix pattern

`DQ_INDEX.md` is GENERATED, never hand-edited, and a pre-commit `--check` blocks stale commits. CLAUDE.md names this explicitly as the anti-rot pattern, with the stale `decisions/README.md` as the named failure mode. **The cure is already in the building; it just was not applied to the ADRs.**

## Proposed shape (to be argued, not adopted as written)

- [ ] **Required ADR frontmatter**: `status` (PROPOSED / ACCEPTED / SUPERSEDED / AMENDED), `supersedes`, `superseded-by`, `amended-by`, `canonical-authority` (which doc wins on conflict).
- [ ] **Admission strictness**: a new ADR must declare what it supersedes, or state `supersedes: none` explicitly. No silent additions.
- [ ] **Generate `decisions/README.md`** from that frontmatter; gate it in pre-commit exactly like the DQ index. Delete the hand-maintained version.
- [ ] **The progressive scan**: a pass over ADR-0001..0018 building a collision matrix -- which pairs disagree, which is later, which is canonical. Well-shaped for a subagent with a strict "cite file:line or say nothing" rule.
- [ ] **Glossary as a standing instrument**: `docs/GLOSSARY.md` exists as of today. Re-running a term-consistency pass after each workshop is cheap and catches this class early.
- [ ] Rule the `L<n>` namespace collision.

## Why now, and why NOT now

**Why it matters now:** today produced more design surface in one morning -- an endgame reframe, an actor want-graph, a glossary, several rulings -- than the ADR set normally absorbs in a month. Pip's own framing: after an explosion of creativity, "bedding down and crispening out" is the next phase. Unbedded creativity contradicts itself faster than anyone can read it.

**Why not now:** it is league week, and this is exactly the kind of interesting work that would eat a freeze. Post-league. Candidate slot: the Saturday retro or the week of 08-03, alongside beacon-internal#15.

## Post-mortem that motivated the filing

The ADR-0016 pack pipeline was recorded as owed in the ADR's own status line and as a prose lane in the runsheet. It was **never given an issue number**. Every single thing built on 2026-07-28 carried one (#996, #1000, #995, #997, #982, #981, #985, #979, #977); the pack did not, so no lane picked it up and it silently did not happen. Documenting debt is not scheduling debt.

issues.title: release: ship a FIRST-RUN.txt in the zip — macOS instructions currently reach nobody who has downloaded
issues.body:
From the website side, 2026-07-29. Pip asked whether the install instructions bundled with the zip could be updated. **They cannot, because there are none.**

## What the release zip actually contains

`godot/export_presets.cfg` sets, on every platform preset:

```
include_filter="build_stamp.txt"
exclude_filter="tests/*, addons/gut/*, tools/*, docs/*, *.md, *.py, *.bat, *.ps1, *.sh, *.xml"
```

`*.md` is excluded, so no README or instructions ship inside the build. A downloader gets the binary and `build_stamp.txt`. Every install instruction we have lives on a web page they have already navigated away from.

## Why this matters right now

The website told macOS users to *"right-click and choose Open"*. **Apple removed that bypass in macOS Sequoia (15.x)** — the context menu now offers only Cancel / Move to Trash. The correct path is System Settings → Privacy & Security → Security → **Open Anyway**.

The first backer of the Manifund funding round hit exactly this on 15.5 today, gave up, and said so publicly — having funded the project without being able to play it. **macOS is ~35% of v0.13.1 downloads** (Windows 7, macOS 6, Linux 4 as of today), so the other five downloaders hit the same wall and did not tell us.

The website copy is fixed (pdoom1-website#195, merged). But a fix on the site does not reach someone who downloaded yesterday and is staring at a Gatekeeper dialog now.

## Ask

Ship a short **`FIRST-RUN.txt`** (or per-platform equivalent) alongside the binary in each release zip:

- **macOS 15+**: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Security → Open Anyway (admin password may be needed). First launch only.
- **macOS 14 and earlier**: right-click / Control-click → Open.
- **Windows**: what SmartScreen shows and how to proceed.
- Where to report a bug (the in-game reporter is **N**), and where to find the leaderboard.

Two implementation notes:
1. `include_filter` already carries `build_stamp.txt`, so the mechanism exists — this is one more filename, not new machinery.
2. **Derive it, do not hand-maintain it.** If the text is typed once per platform it will rot exactly as the website copy did. Generating it at build time from a single source, and having the website render the same source, means one edit fixes both surfaces. That also lets the file carry the version it shipped with, so a stale copy is self-identifying.

## The real fix, for the record

Signing + notarisation via the Apple Developer Program removes the dialog entirely. That is a budget line rather than a code change, and Pip has flagged it as a funded item. `FIRST-RUN.txt` is the interim that costs nothing.

Related: pdoom1#1011 (keybind docs), pdoom1-website#195.

issues.title: design(content): provenance real infrastructure failure modes into the event history as flavour text / metadata
issues.body:
Captured from Pip, 2026-07-29, mid-league-week. **Idea capture only -- he flagged "will solve in more detail later I think there might be notes", so search for those notes before designing anything here.**

> "encountered some funny failure modes I want to provenance into the game's event history as the equivalent of flavour text / metadata"

## What this is

While building the game and its surrounding infrastructure, the project keeps hitting genuinely funny, genuinely instructive failure modes -- CI that reported green while running zero tests, a workflow whose only protection from publishing to a live website was a missing Python import, a README advertising a download that had never existed, a leaderboard that forked every time the music changed. These are real artifacts of trying to build a thing carefully.

The idea is to **provenance** them into the game's own event history as flavour text or metadata, rather than letting them evaporate into commit messages.

## Why it is more than a joke

The game's thesis is that holding back catastrophe is an operational problem: attention, coordination, and the slow accumulation of things nobody had time to check. **The project's own failure modes are instances of the thing the game is about.** A safety lab whose monitoring silently reports green is not a gag -- it is the game's premise, observed in the wild, at small scale, by the person building it.

That is a rare kind of authenticity and it cannot be manufactured later.

## Open questions for the actual design pass

- **Surface.** In-game flavour text on events? A metadata field on event records? An appendix/credits surface? A website page? These have very different content and hygiene requirements.
- **Reality-tether hygiene.** `RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md` and the ADR-0016 pack discipline keep the reality lane strictly factual and the fiction lane separate. Self-referential project history is a THIRD category and needs an explicit ruling on which lane it belongs to, or it will contaminate one of them.
- **Attribution.** These failures have authors, including agents. Naming is fine when self-deprecating and the author consents; be careful about anything that reads as blame.
- **Dosage.** The ~1-2 beats/month anchor from the failure-mode content discipline probably applies here too. Too much and the game is winking at itself constantly.
- **Does it belong in the ladder-affecting content at all?** If it is pure flavour, it must not change what happens on a fixed seed, or it forks the ladder.

## First step

Find Pip's notes. He believes they exist. Do not design against this issue's paraphrase when the source may be better.

issues.title: positioning: the AI-generated-art immune reaction is a reputational risk, not just an art-quality one
issues.body:
Raised by Austin Chen on the Manifund page (2026-07-29), alongside a $1,000 donation:

> "I'd also worry that the game currently looks a little bit too AI-generated and/or chaotic, per the screenshots. I'm generally a fan of AI assistance, but specifically the gaming community has a strong immune reaction against AI content, and also in this case I'd worry there's just too much slop all around. Possibly pairing with a good visual/graphic designer might be quite helpful, since games especially seem to have high standards/stakes for visual appeal to be successful."

Pip's reply, which is the project's current public position:

> "I've held off on the UX and UI as long as I can in the dev cycle deliberately, because I can iterate much faster through game engines than quality art, and that's where my main budget expenses will mostly emerge. Consider the visual assets very much placeholders and proof-of-concepts for now and they will iterate rapidly, then start to stabilise as I settle on art direction and start getting real assets designed."

## Why file this separately from the existing art issues

#850 (coherence + dedup pass), #900 (art ramp), #903 (icon set) all treat this as an art-QUALITY problem. Austin is describing something different: **an audience-reaction problem.** The gaming community's response to visible AI art is not proportional to the art's quality -- it is closer to a categorical rejection. Improving the art does not, by itself, address it.

Two distinct failure modes, and this project's own risk register already names the first:

1. *"People might take AI safety less seriously due to this game being low-status or failing in reputationally damaging ways"* -- straight from the Manifund application's failure-modes section. Visible AI slop is a concrete route to exactly that.
2. Prospective players bounce off screenshots before they ever reach the design, which is the part that is actually good.

## The asymmetry worth acting on

**The placeholder status is currently invisible.** Someone looking at screenshots has no way to know the art is scaffolding rather than the shipped intent -- so they price it as the finished product. Saying so, publicly and in-context, is nearly free and converts "slop" into "work in progress", which reads completely differently.

This is now also a **public commitment**: the Manifund application states funding will pay "human artists to replace current AI-generated assets".

## Candidate actions, cheapest first

- [ ] Label generated assets as placeholder where players and funders actually look: website screenshots caption, README, itch/store copy if any.
- [ ] Make sure website copy does not present generated art as final (raised in pdoom1-website #194).
- [ ] Prioritise the coherence/dedup pass (#850) -- "chaotic" is partly a consistency problem, and consistency is achievable without human artists.
- [ ] Budget line already exists for a directed human-artist pass; Austin's specific suggestion is pairing with a visual/graphic designer rather than commissioning piecework.
- [ ] Consider whether screenshots used for FUNDING audiences should be chosen for legibility over spectacle.

## Note

Do not over-correct into hiding the tooling. The project is honest about how it is built, and the application is explicit. The fix is labelling and coherence, not concealment.

issues.title: deploy(web): playable browser demo via Godot HTML5 export -- lower the try-it barrier to zero
issues.body:
Raised by Austin Chen on the Manifund page (2026-07-29), alongside a $1,000 donation:

> "I'd encourage Pip to see if Godot or Claude can port at least a demo, to be directly playable on web/mobile."

He raised it because he could not get the macOS build to launch (see #917) and gave up. That is the strongest possible argument for this issue: **a funder who wanted to play, could not, and stopped trying.** Every install step is a place people leave.

## Why this is plausible here

- Godot 4.5 exports to HTML5/WebAssembly natively.
- The game is turn-based with no realtime or physics load -- close to the best-case profile for a web export.
- There is an existing `pdoom1-webclient` TypeScript prototype (Feb 2026) that may or may not be relevant; check before starting from scratch.

## Known unknowns, to scope before committing

- **Build size.** The `.pck` is ~60MB; a web build that takes minutes to load defeats the purpose. Needs measuring, and likely a trimmed demo-only asset set.
- **Leaderboard submission from the browser.** The score API is token-authed; a web client changes the trust model, and an easily-forged submission path would poison the ladder. **This must not be bolted on casually** -- see #1012 on leaderboard integrity.
- **Save/config persistence** moves to browser storage.
- **A demo is not the game.** Scope deliberately: a bounded run, maybe a fixed seed, clearly labelled as a demo, with the desktop build as the real thing.

## Deliberately NOT this issue

Mobile. Pip's own note: *"I am probably culturally biased against mobile games so that is definitely a blindspot of mine."* A blindspot is worth naming, but touch UI for a dense strategy interface is a separate and much larger design problem. Web-on-desktop first.

## Sequencing

Post-league. This is a real lane, not a quick fix, and it competes with signing (#683) -- which fixes the same underlying problem ("people cannot run the game") more cheaply for the desktop audience that already exists.

issues.title: deploy: robust cross-OS releases (Windows/Linux/macOS) by next Epoch

milestone.title: First Contact
milestone.description: ARC (theme milestone, ~quarterly). Launch-hardening: legibility, onboarding, hotpatches, early-game depth. Spans the v0.13.x..~v0.15 monthly epochs. Nomenclature: docs/RELEASE_NOMENCLATURE.md

issues.body:
Pip ruling 2026-07-26: deployments must be robust across OSs by the next Epoch.

## Evidence from the v0.13.1 release (2026-07-26)
- The Enhanced Release CI workflow now builds all 3 platforms on tag push (new since v0.13.0), but packages ONLY exe+pck: **no gdextension binaries (godotsteam), no HOW-TO-RUN.txt**. Verified on Windows: game boots but GDExtension fails to load (3 errors) and Steam integration is silently dead.
- v0.13.1 Windows assets were hand-replaced with a complete, stamp-verified local build under the CI's canonical names. Linux zip patched with its .so. macOS .app untested/unverified.
- Pre-Release Checks workflow fails on missing CHANGELOG entry (process gap, being fixed).

## Definition of robust (proposed)
1. CI packaging includes per-platform gdextension binaries + HOW-TO-RUN.txt (immediate fix in flight).
2. Boot-test matrix: each platform zip verified to launch to menu (manual friend-confirmations first -- macOS + Debian testers standing by; automate headless boot smoke later).
3. Release notes carry honest per-platform test status ('boots on X, not extensively tested') until a platform graduates.
4. Signing/trust posture documented per platform (SmartScreen / Gatekeeper unidentified-developer / chmod +x).
5. RELEASE_CHECKLIST.md covers all platforms; Pre-Release Checks green on tag.

Related: #775 (release-branch model), the launch packaging notes (zip-extract trap), today's session findings.

issues.title: leaderboard integrity: no dev-mode/verification field reaches a submitted score, so the website cannot filter on it
issues.body:
Filed from the website side during league-week prep, 2026-07-29. Pip asked us to check whether dev-mode use is already distinguished on scores, and to request it be surfaced **programmatically** so pdoom1-website can filter during sweeps rather than by eye.

## What we found

**There is no dev-mode or integrity field on a submitted score.** Read live from the production API today, a submitted entry carries exactly:

```
baseline_doom_integral, baseline_score, date, doom_integral, duration_seconds,
entry_uuid, game_mode, level_reached, player_name, score
```

No taint flag, no verification hash, no build-provenance field.

**But an anti-cheat design does exist** — it just does not reach the leaderboard:

- `godot/autoload/verification_tracker.gd` — a hash chain, described in-file as *"anti-cheat, share format, and bug-repro in one"*.
- `godot/scripts/core/replay_simulator.gd` — *"the canonical artifact -- anti-cheat, share format, and bug-repro in one"*, with *"the sound anti-cheat property: you cannot claim a score higher than"* the replay reproduces.

Replay verification is a **stronger** property than a dev-mode flag, because it is outcome-based rather than trust-based. The gap is that neither the hash nor any derived verdict is attached to the submitted entry, so nothing downstream can act on it.

## Why this is live right now

`BuildInfo.DEV_BUILD` is `const DEV_BUILD := true` (`build_info.gd:18`) — a hand-flipped constant with **no writer anywhere in the build tooling** (grepped `.py`/`.yml`/`.sh`/`.cfg`; `tools/build_release.py` passes `--export-release`, which does not touch a GDScript const). So a shipped release carries whatever was committed at the cut, and **backslash currently opens the full dev overlay in public builds**, including pokes that set money, compute and doom.

A new league opens **Fri 2026-07-31 ~1700 AEST on L3**. Until then, a score set with dev pokes is indistinguishable from a legitimate one, at every layer.

## What the website needs

Not a redesign — one field, and the ability to read it:

1. **An integrity verdict on the submitted entry.** Whatever shape suits the game: a boolean, an enum (`verified` / `unverified` / `dev-assisted`), or the replay hash plus a server-side check. The website is a read-only consumer per #679 and will not compute its own.
2. **Build provenance on the entry** — at minimum whether `DEV_BUILD` was true for the binary that produced the score. That is cheap and answers the immediate question even before replay verification is wired through.
3. **The field exposed on the GET path**, so a website sweep can filter programmatically. Right now we would have to filter by eye, which does not scale and will not happen.

Related and worth deciding together: `DEV_BUILD` having no writer means the flag is set by whoever last edited the file. If it were derived at build time, field 2 becomes trustworthy rather than advisory.

## Pip's other ask, game-side

> "We should make that text explicit, particularly in the onboarding sections for new players."

Onboarding should state plainly what dev mode does to score validity — before a player uses it, not after. A player who discovers their run does not count *after* a 6-8 hour session has had a bad time that was entirely preventable with one sentence.

## Context from the website side

We preserved **27 real submissions from 6 players** (2026-07-19 to 2026-07-26) that never reached the site because of a separate seed/version key mismatch — captured at `public/leaderboard/data/preserved/2026-07-29-orphaned-boards/`. Those are being surfaced as clearly-labelled pre-epoch history and will not be merged forward. Mentioned because it is the same class of problem: something true about a score that no consumer could see.

Related: pdoom1-website#151 (board keys, L3 cut), pdoom1#1011 (keybind docs + `DEV_BUILD` gating).

issues.title: feat(engine): integrate frontier-labs dataset (pdoom-data#37); expose a list the website can pull to fix calculate-game-stats
issues.body:
## Ask (follow-on from pdoom-data#37)

Once pdoom-data ships its first-pass frontier-labs dataset (**PipFoweraker/pdoom-data#37** — foundation dates 2000→present), build the follow-on:

1. **Integrate** the frontier-labs list + foundation dates into the game engine (labs as timeline entities that come into existence on their founding dates).
2. **As soon as the MVP is enough for the website to consume it**, expose it so pdoom1-website can pull the list — so we can retire the hardcoded lab list in `calculate-game-stats.py` and drive `frontier_labs_count` (and future stats) from real data.

## Why

pdoom1-website currently hardcodes the frontier-labs list in `scripts/calculate-game-stats.py` to produce a stubbed count. Per the cross-repo protocol (game/data own truth; the website derives), that count should come from the canonical dataset. This also feeds the website's planned "state of doom" stats page.

## Sequencing (please don't block the website on full engine work)

`pdoom-data#37` → **engine integration** → **expose a consumable artifact**. The website does **not** need the full engine integration — it just needs a **stable, fetchable list** of `{id, name, founded, status}`. Please ship that consumable early (a served JSON, or simply point us at the pdoom-data serveable if that's cleaner) even if the richer engine timeline mechanics land later.

## Definition of done (for the website's needs)

- A documented, fetchable artifact of frontier labs + foundation dates.
- The URL + shape noted in a comment here so the pdoom1-website session can wire `calculate-game-stats.py` to it.

---
_Depends on pdoom-data#37. Filed as cross-repo work at Pip's direction (contact-protocol override, 2026-07-27) by the pdoom1-website session._

issues.title: docs+emit(keybinds): three docs disagree with keybind_manager.gd; emit a keybind artifact so the website derives instead of mirroring
issues.body:
## Two things, one root cause

The website now publishes in-game bug-reporting guidance on <https://pdoom1.com/bug-report/> (pdoom1-website PR for `content/bug-report-in-game-guidance`). Writing it surfaced that **the repo's own docs disagree with `keybind_manager.gd` about which key opens the bug reporter**, and that there is no machine-readable place for a downstream consumer to get the answer.

A new league opens Fri 2026-07-31 on a fresh build, so bug reports are about to spike — a wrong key in a doc is a player pressing nothing, seeing nothing happen, and concluding the game is broken.

---

### 1. Stale keybind references (small, mechanical)

Authoritative source, `godot/autoload/keybind_manager.gd`:

```gdscript
"bug_reporter": {"key": KEY_N,         "category": Category.UI,    "description": "Open Bug Reporter"},
"dev_mode":     {"key": KEY_BACKSLASH, "category": Category.DEBUG, "description": "Toggle Dev Mode Overlay"},
```

with the in-file comment *"Moved off backslash to N (N already opened the bug reporter) -- backslash is now DEV MODE."*

Disagreeing references found:

| File | Line | Says | Correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CONTRIBUTING.md` | 213 | "press **\\** (backslash) in-game to open the built-in bug reporter" | `N` |
| `CHANGELOG.md` | 188 | "Press F8 or backslash to report bugs during gameplay" | historical entry — see note |
| `README.md` | 39 | "Press **`N`**" | already correct, no change |

`CHANGELOG.md:188` is a historical release entry, so rewriting it would falsify history. Suggest leaving the text and appending a parenthetical like `(bind later moved to N)`, rather than editing the record.

`CONTRIBUTING.md:213` also claims the reporter "automatically captures game state". What it actually captures (`godot/scripts/core/bug_reporter.gd::collect_system_info`) is OS name, Godot version, game version and a UTC timestamp — plus an optional screenshot and save-file copy behind tick boxes. Not game state. Worth correcting in the same pass.

---

### 2. The ask: emit a keybind artifact per release

**The website currently mirrors, and a mirror rots.** `scripts/sync/sync-keybinds.py` in pdoom1-website parses `keybind_manager.gd` out of a *local checkout* and writes `public/data/keybinds.json`, which the page renders from. That file is explicitly stamped `"mirror": true` with the source path, source commit and a `verified_on` date, and a `--check` mode fails the build on drift, on a mirror older than 90 days, and on any key typed literally into the HTML. That is the best the website can do unilaterally — but it depends on someone having a pdoom1 checkout, so it degrades to an age check in CI.

**Request:** publish the default keybinds as a release artifact, the way `version.json` already works for platform availability. Per the cross-repo protocol, this should be an artifact a workflow can consume, not prose a human copies — the doc drift above is exactly what happens when the answer only exists as prose.

Shape that would work (the website already consumes this schema, so matching it costs nothing downstream):

```json
{
  "version": 1,
  "game_version": "0.13.2",
  "source_commit": "4293eee",
  "generated_at": "2026-07-31T00:00:00Z",
  "dev_build": false,
  "keybinds": [
    {
      "action": "bug_reporter",
      "godot_keycode": "KEY_N",
      "key": "N",
      "modifiers": [],
      "category": "ui",
      "description": "Open Bug Reporter",
      "availability": "all_builds"
    },
    {
      "action": "dev_mode",
      "godot_keycode": "KEY_BACKSLASH",
      "key": "\\",
      "modifiers": [],
      "category": "debug",
      "description": "Toggle Dev Mode Overlay",
      "availability": "dev_build_only"
    }
  ]
}
```

Notes on the fields that matter most:

- **`availability`** — please distinguish `all_builds` from `dev_build_only`. This is not derivable from `category`: `debug_overlay` is category DEBUG but is **not** gated (`godot/scripts/debug/debug_overlay.gd:40` connects unconditionally), whereas `dev_mode`, `flight_recorder` and `ui_evolution_shot` all return early unless `BuildInfo.is_dev_build()`. The website had to hand-maintain that distinction by reading each handler, which is precisely the thing that will drift.
- **`dev_build`** — the value of `BuildInfo.DEV_BUILD` *in the build being shipped*. See the flag note below; without this the site cannot honestly tell a player whether dev mode exists in their download.
- **`key`** — the `OS.get_keycode_string()` rendering. The website currently reimplements that mapping in Python and refuses to guess on an unknown constant; emitting it from Godot removes the reimplementation.

Generating it is cheap — `KeybindManager.keybinds` is already a plain dictionary, so a small export script or a GUT-run dump could write it at package time and attach it to the release.

---

### 3. Side observation: `BuildInfo.DEV_BUILD` is a hand-flipped constant

`godot/scripts/core/build_info.gd:18` is `const DEV_BUILD := true`, and nothing in `tools/build_release.py` or any workflow flips it — I grepped `--include=*.py --include=*.yml --include=*.sh --include=*.cfg` and found no writer. The docstring says to "flip to false for a clean release cut", which makes it a manual step with no guard.

So as things stand, a shipped release build has whatever value was committed, and **backslash currently opens the full dev-mode overlay in a public build** (state readout plus pokes that set money/compute/doom). That may well be intentional for alpha — flagging it rather than assuming, since it is one uncommitted edit away from being either state and nothing verifies which.

The website page is written to be true under both values ("it may or may not be present in your build; if the key does nothing, your build has it off"), so nothing is blocked on this. But if you want the site to state it definitively, that is what the `dev_build` field above is for.

---

### Related

- #994 (`feat(emit): calibration artifact`) is the same shape of ask — game emits a machine-readable artifact so the website consumes instead of guessing. If you are building emit infrastructure for that, this could ride along.
- #777 (in-game screenshot flow, `[`) and #602 (navigation audit / mirrored toggle keys) both touch binds that would appear in this artifact.

_Filed from the website side while writing the in-game reporting guidance._

issues.title: devblog automation: repair as a draft-generator (never auto-publish) -- post-league
issues.body:
Stacked for **after the Fri 2026-07-31 league launch**. Split out of the freeze-morning CI triage on 2026-07-29.

## Ruling that scopes this (Pip, 2026-07-29)

> "I dont want autogenerated devblog posts to be publiished, but the content is very usful for the publishing pipeline."

So this is NOT "make the workflow work again". The generator's *output* is wanted as raw material for human-authored posts; the *publishing* half must stay off permanently.

## What was done already (the holding fix)

`.github/workflows/dev-blog-automation.yml` is now **workflow_dispatch only** -- the `push: [main]` and `pull_request: [closed]` triggers were removed. That cleared a red that was firing on every single run of every branch and was drowning the "is CI green" signal on freeze day.

## Why the obvious two-line fix was refused

The visible failure is one missing dependency:

- `analyze-changes` installs `gitpython` (line 60).
- `create-dev-blog-entry` is a separate runner, sets up Python, then runs `import git` with no install step -> `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'git'`.

But that error is the only thing that has ever stopped this workflow from publishing:

1. `create-dev-blog-entry` ends in `git push` to `main`.
2. That push matches `sync-dev-blog.yml`'s `paths: dev-blog/entries/**` trigger.
3. `sync-dev-blog.yml` checks out `PipFoweraker/pdoom1-website` with `WEBSITE_SYNC_TOKEN` and pushes to its `main`.

Net: installing gitpython would have started auto-posting to the live public site on every merge.

## Second defect, never caught because the first one masks it

The entry body is built from triple-quoted strings indented inside a heredoc (roughly lines 218-274 pre-edit). Every emitted line carries 8 leading spaces, so the YAML frontmatter does not parse and the whole post renders as a single code block. The workflow has never produced an entry, so this has never been observed in the wild. The 50 files in `dev-blog/entries/` are human-authored (`git log -- dev-blog/` shows session captures and the music-session writeup, not automation output).

## Proposed shape

- [ ] Add the missing dependency install to `create-dev-blog-entry`.
- [ ] Fix the indent-mangled frontmatter/body generation; add a test or a golden-file check so a malformed entry cannot pass silently.
- [ ] **Remove the `git push` entirely.** Emit the generated material as a workflow artifact (or into a gitignored/scratch path), never a commit.
- [ ] Do NOT re-add the automatic `push`/`pull_request` triggers.
- [ ] Decide where the drafts land so they are genuinely usable as publishing-pipeline input rather than another thing to go stale.
- [ ] Replace `os.system('cd dev-blog && python generate_index.py')` with a checked subprocess call.

## Related

Rhymes with #1008 (release feed index is generated as an artifact and never committed back, so it is hand-maintained in practice). Both are "generated content that was meant to flow automatically, does not, and the gap got papered over by hand" -- worth a shared decision on which generated artifacts are allowed to auto-commit and which are draft-only.

issues.title: Release feed index is hand-maintained in practice: generated feed is uploaded as an artifact, never committed back
issues.body:
## Symptom

`public/releases/releases.json` (tracked) drifts from reality. Two instances found:

- v0.9.0 listed after the GitHub release was deleted (pruned by hand in #1006).
- v0.13.0 and v0.13.1 **missing** from the index despite both being tagged and released.

#1006 fixed the first instance by hand. This issue is the generator fix so it stops recurring.

## Root cause

`scripts/generate_release_metadata.py` rebuilds the ENTIRE index from git tags on every
run (`generate_releases_index`, line ~277) -- so CI already computes the correct index.
But `.github/workflows/enhanced-release.yml:213` only does `actions/upload-artifact` with
`path: public/releases/`. The correct feed is produced as a **build artifact and thrown
away**; nothing ever commits it back to the repo.

Net effect: the tracked index is hand-maintained, which is the documented rot anti-pattern
(cf. `docs/game-design/DQ_INDEX.md`, which is generated + gated by a `--check` pre-commit
hook -- that is the pattern to copy).

## Second defect: the detector is muted

`enhanced-release.yml:367-374` runs `verify_release_urls.py --sweep` with
`continue-on-error: true`. That is the same green-when-red mechanism PR #1007 just removed
from the simulation-tests job, one scope down at step level. The sweep also only runs
during a release workflow, so rot arising between releases is invisible until the next tag.

## Suggested fix (not prescriptive)

1. Commit the generated feed back on tag (or, cheaper and more in-house-style: add
   `generate_release_metadata.py --check` as a pre-commit + CI gate that fails when the
   tracked index differs from what the generator produces -- mirrors `sync_version.py --check`
   and `generate_dq_index.py --check`).
2. Make the `--sweep` step visible: either drop `continue-on-error` or surface its output
   the way #1007 surfaces sim-tier red. An old release 404ing should not block a NEW tag
   from shipping, so if it stays non-blocking it must at least be loudly reported.
3. Backfill v0.13.0/v0.13.1 into the index as part of the next version bump.

Found during the 2026-07-28 GitHub hygiene sweep; flagged (not silently regenerated) by the
#1006 lane.
